original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,3,2), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every three points determine at least two distinct distances, equivalently a set with no equilateral triangles.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the local-properties open problem on ϕ(n,k,l): after defining ϕ(n,k,l) for planar n-point sets in which every k-point subset determines at least l distinct distances, the paper specializes to k=3, identifies ϕ(n,3,2) with forbidding equilateral triangles, and states the official problem: "Find the asymptotic value of ϕ(n,3,2)." ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right target quantity ϕ(n,3,2), the correct local condition "every three points determine at least two distinct distances," the paper’s equivalent reformulation in terms of excluding equilateral triangles, and the right objective of determining its asymptotic value. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that the minimum is over all n-point sets P with P ⊂ ℝ^2.
Specify that the distances are Euclidean pairwise distances determined by pairs of points of P.
Clarify that "every three points" means every 3-point subset of P, i.e. three distinct points of P.
Define ϕ(n,k,l) itself, since the stand-alone question should not assume the notation is already known.
Say explicitly that the asymptotic question is about the growth of ϕ(n,3,2) as n → ∞.
Use the paper’s phrasing "do not span any equilateral triangles" if you want the wording to track the paper exactly.
refined_question: As n → ∞, determine the asymptotic growth of ϕ(n,3,2), where for positive integers n,k,l, ϕ(n,k,l) denotes the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P ⊂ ℝ^2 such that every k-point subset of P determines at least l distinct distances; equivalently here, determine the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set that does not span any equilateral triangles. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Determine, as a function of n, the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P ⊂ ℝ^2 that does not span any equilateral triangles. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. The relevant section first defines ϕ(n,k,l) for planar point sets with a local distance condition, then treats the case k=3 and explicitly states that ϕ(n,3,2) is the minimum number of distinct distances determined by a set of n points that do not span any equilateral triangles, and immediately poses the open problem of finding its asymptotic value. The refined question keeps exactly that scope and only makes explicit the ambient space ℝ^2, the minimization domain, the meaning of the notation, and the asymptotic variable. The same passage also records the bounds Ω(n/log n) and O(n/√log n), showing that the paper views this as a distinct-distances asymptotics problem rather than a broader structural variant. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
